title: Enterprise VC
primary_theme: Early-stage enterprise investing with founder conviction
founder_lessons: Early enterprise investing often means backing founders before their idea is complete, as long as they have domain insight and conviction.
The best enterprise founders can build a compelling story about the problem they are solving, even in a category few people understand.
Use your network of customers to validate whether a founder is adding real value and can be a reliable partner over time.
Supporting founders through company formation and the first rounds can create an unfair long-term advantage.
notable_quotes: If it's a first time founder working on a category that not everyone knows about, I think what I find really valuable is founders being able to build on their story a little bit.
The earliest is as early as founders thinking about starting something. And we've often led the rounds before any other investors participated.
We also then involve other customers that are in our network to see if we can understand if we can help them down the road.
